You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Marvell FY2027 Q2 Highlights: Revenue $2.74B, Up 37% YoY; Full-Year Outlook Raised, Shares Still Drop ~8% After Hours

TEXT:
Key Takeaways
Marvell Technology reported FY2027 Q2 results (quarter ended August 1, 2026) with revenue of $2.739 billion, up about 36.5%–37% year over year and 13% sequentially. That was $39 million above the midpoint of the guidance issued on May 27, 2026, and slightly above Street estimates of about $2.71–$2.72 billion. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.94, up 40% from $0.67 a year earlier and a touch above estimates of about $0.92–$0.93. GAAP net income was $308.0 million, or $0.33 per diluted share. Data center revenue was $2.172 billion, up 46% year over year and 18% sequentially, and accounted for 79% of total sales. Non-GAAP gross margin was 58.9%, down 0.5 percentage point from a year earlier.
Management raised its FY2027 revenue outlook to about $12 billion (roughly +45% year over year, from about $11.5 billion previously) and its FY2028 revenue outlook to about $18 billion (roughly +50%, from about $16.5 billion previously). Data center revenue is expected to grow about 60% in FY2028. Q3 guidance midpoint is $3.15 billion (±5%) for revenue and $1.10 (±$0.05) for non-GAAP EPS, both above then-prevailing Wall Street estimates. Despite the beats and raises, the stock fell as much as about 7.8% after hours to around $222.62. The market’s focus shifted to timing: custom silicon ramps in the second half, and the larger Google-related contribution is framed more as an FY2029-and-beyond story.
1. Overall Revenue and Profitability
Revenue $2.739 billion , +36.5%–37% year over year, +13% quarter over quarter; a quarterly record and $39 million above the prior Q2 guide midpoint.
Non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.94 , +40% year over year (from $0.67) and up from $0.80 in Q1.
GAAP diluted EPS $0.33 ; GAAP net income $308.0 million; non-GAAP net income $865.9 million.
GAAP gross margin 53.1%; non-GAAP gross margin 58.9% (59.4% a year earlier).
GAAP operating income $459.7 million, operating margin 16.8% ; non-GAAP operating income $1.003 billion, operating margin 36.6% (+180 bps year over year, +160 bps sequentially).
Operating cash flow $605.5 million ; capex about $126.7 million, implying free cash flow of roughly $479 million.
Cash and cash equivalents $3.933 billion as of August 1, 2026. The company bought back $200 million of stock and paid about $53.9 million in dividends during the quarter.

2. Data Center Performance
Data center revenue $2.172 billion , +46% year over year and +18% sequentially, or 79% of total sales (74% a year earlier; 76% in Q1). That beat the LSEG economist estimate of about $2.13 billion.
Chairman and CEO Matt Murphy said growth was broad-based across the data center portfolio: connectivity demand is strong, and the custom business is expected to accelerate significantly beginning in the second half of FY2027 .
Management expects data center custom silicon to ramp sharply in 2H FY2027 and more than double year over year in FY2028 . Growth is expected from XPUs and XPU-adjacent products, including CXL and custom networking.
On the call, management confirmed an 8-K disclosure of an expanded commercial agreement and related warrants with a major hyperscaler. Analysts identified the partner as Google. Murphy said the work covers programs already underway, newly won designs, and potential future programs, spanning AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, NICs, memory-interface controllers, and near-memory compute products attached to the TPU ecosystem.
Murphy said the agreement and other new programs increase management’s confidence that custom silicon revenue will be “meaningfully larger” in FY2029 and the years after . More long-term detail is slated for Investor Day on October 6, 2026.
3. Other End Markets
Communications and other revenue $567.8 million , +10% year over year and -3% sequentially, or 21% of sales (26% a year earlier).
This segment is no longer the growth engine and continues to shrink as a share of the mix.
Management highlighted CXL memory expansion as increasingly important for AI inference deployments; Marvell said it has won additional designs as customers reshape memory architectures amid tight memory supply.
4. Capital Allocation and Forward Plans
Operating cash flow was $605.5 million in the quarter; $200 million was returned via buybacks and about $53.9 million via dividends.
Period-end snapshot: total assets $27.555 billion, long-term debt $4.963 billion, stockholders’ equity $18.532 billion.
FY2027 revenue outlook raised to about $12 billion (~+45% YoY) from about $11.5 billion.
[...]
The Google-related agreement has been described in coverage as a potential ~$120 billion opportunity through FY2033, with equity ownership of up to about $12.2 billion. Management, however, pointed to a meaningfully larger custom-silicon scale in FY2029 and beyond , which the market read as “too far out to re-rate the stock today.”
[...]
October 6 Investor Day is the next checkpoint. Unless management pulls the custom ramp, Google recognition timing, and margin path closer and more specific, multiple compression can linger.
[...]
One-line conclusion: This is a “beat-and-raise on paper, but custom and the Google scale-up still sit further out” print. Near-term price action hinges on whether investors prize the $12B / $18B raises more than the wait for custom silicon to show up in the run-rate.
